title: Tensor and compact-support coherence before duality
statement:
Let $A=A_{E,n}$, with $\ell\ne p$ [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories of constant-$A$ modules on small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], derived tensor [def-kun-derived-tensor], exact inverse image, and compact-support direct image given by proper direct image after open extension by zero [def-amb-etale-compact-support]. Consider either (i) separated finite-type schemes over an excellent strictly henselian equal-characteristic-$p$ trait $B$ with algebraically closed residue field, with $T_Z=\Psi_Z=i_Z^*R\bar j_{Z*}$ from the geometric generic fibre to the closed fibre, or (ii) separated finite-type schemes over an algebraically closed characteristic-$p$ field $F$, a separably closed extension $K/F$, and $T_Z=q_Z^*$ for $q_Z:Z_K\to Z$. A prime on a morphism denotes its closed fibre in (i), or its $K$-base change in (ii). Write $h$ for its source-fibre morphism: $h=u_{\bar\eta}:X_{\bar\eta}\to Y_{\bar\eta}$ in (i), $h=u$ in (ii). In the formulas below, an unprimed $u^*$, $Ru_*$, $Ru_!$, $\mathrm{PF}_u$, $\mu_u$ or $\epsilon_u$ applied on the source fibres (to the right of, or inside, $T$) denotes the corresponding operation for $h$. In (i), a trait is the spectrum of a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], excellence means excellence of affine coordinate rings [def-exc-excellent-ring], and strictly henselian has the meaning of [def-weil-pbc-henselian-terminology].

For each $u:X\to Y$, let $b_u:u'^*T_Y\to T_Xu^*$ be ordinary exchange, $C_u:Ru'_!T_X\to T_YRu_!$ compact-support exchange, and $t_Z:T_ZM\otimes T_ZN\to T_Z(M\otimes N)$ the lax tensor map (in (ii) the tensor isomorphism). In (i), $C_u$ is the compact-support exchange defined by compactification and the $\bar j^*\dashv R\bar j_*$ counit, as in [def-trf-deformation-specialization]. In (ii), it is the inverse compact-support base-change map. These maps are defined on the ambient derived categories for these schemes, including when the tensor products are unbounded below. They preserve shifts and their natural transformations are compatible with the derived cone models. One has $T_{\operatorname{Spec} F}A=A$ in (ii) and $\Psi_BA=A$ in (i).

For proper $u$, ordinary exchange $e_u:T_YRu_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Ru'_*T_X$ is invertible and $C_u=e_u^{-1}$ under $Ru_!=Ru_*$. For smooth $u$, $b_u$ is invertible on bounded constructible inputs [def-weil-pbc-constructible-complexes]. All these exchanges, and their inverses where specified, respect identities and composition. The composition formula is
$$C_{vu}=C_v(Ru_!(-))\circ Rv'_!(C_u)$$
under compact-support composition. Write $\mathrm{PF}_u:Ru_!M\otimes N\to Ru_!(M\otimes u^*N)$ for the canonical compact-support projection map: on a compactification $u=rj$ ($j$ open, $r$ proper), with its base change for $u'$, it is the proper projection map $\mathrm{PF}_r(j_!M,N):Rr_*j_!M\otimes N\to Rr_*(j_!M\otimes r^*N)$ of [def-kun-projection-formula-map] followed by $Rr_*$ of the open tensor comparison $j_!M\otimes r^*N\xrightarrow{\sim}j_!(M\otimes j^*r^*N)$ of [lem-pur-etale-open-derived-tensor] and $j^*r^*=u^*$; for proper $u$ ($j=\mathrm{id}$) it is $\mathrm{PF}_u$ of [def-kun-projection-formula-map]. The equation below holds for every such compactification. Under the canonical tensor and pullback associations,
$$C_u(M\otimes u^*N)\circ Ru'_!\bigl(t_X\circ(1\otimes b_u)\bigr)\circ\mathrm{PF}_{u'}
=T_Y(\mathrm{PF}_u)\circ t_Y\circ(C_u(M)\otimes1).$$
Both sides map $Ru'_!T_XM\otimes T_YN$ to $T_YRu_!(M\otimes u^*N)$. Moreover $b_u$ is monoidal, namely
$$b_u(M\otimes N)\circ u'^*t_Y=t_X\circ(b_u(M)\otimes b_u(N)),$$
and proper exchange is monoidal with respect to the ordinary direct-image lax tensor maps $\mu_u$:
$$e_u(M\otimes N)\circ T_Y\mu_u\circ t_Y
=Ru'_*t_X\circ\mu_{u'}\circ(e_u(M)\otimes e_u(N)).$$
For the ordinary counit $\epsilon_u:u^*Ru_*\to1$ and proper $u$,
$$\epsilon_{u'}\circ u'^*e_u=T_X\epsilon_u\circ b_u(Ru_*(-)).$$
These are identities of the specified canonical maps, not invertibility assertions for $t_Z$.

In (i), passage to reduced schemes and finite dominant extensions of strictly henselian traits, with chosen compatible geometric generic points, gives canonical identifications of $T,b,C,t,e$ and their composition maps. In (ii) they are compatible with towers of separably closed extensions and reduction of schemes. No change of the coefficient ring is meant by reduction here.

proof.text: Fix all coefficients once and for all. The constant-$A$ inverse images are exact left adjoints and are strong monoidal on the unbounded derived categories. The canonical composition identifications are monoidal and associative. For each inverse image $L$ with right adjoint $R$, equip $R$ with the lax tensor map whose adjunct is $LRM\otimes LRN\xrightarrow{\epsilon_M\otimes\epsilon_N}M\otimes N$. The monoidal-adjunction statements show that these tensor maps have monoidal units and counits. Thus $T=i^*R\bar j_*$ has precisely the indicated lax tensor map, and $T=q^*$ has its strong tensor map. This construction does not assert that the tensor map for nearby cycles is invertible.

source.place: Tags 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product), 0D6E (lemma-derived-pushforward-composition); adjunction definition of the right-adjoint tensor map

proof.text:
Use $\bar j_Z:Z_{\bar\eta}\to Z$ as a scheme morphism, not as an open immersion. Define $b_u$ by applying $i_X^*$ to the ordinary square mate for $u,\bar j$, with pullback composition. For compact support choose a Nagata compactification of $u$. The unbounded compact-support comparison theorem makes its functor independent of that choice and supplies exchange along $i$ and along $\bar j$. Write $B_{u,v}:v^*Ru_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Ru_{v!}v_X^*$ for those exchanges. Define $d_u:Ru_!R\bar j_{X*}\to R\bar j_{Y*}Rh_!$ to be adjoint under $\bar j_Y^*\dashv R\bar j_{Y*}$ to
$$\bar j_Y^*Ru_!R\bar j_{X*}\xrightarrow{B_{u,\bar j_Y}}Rh_!\bar j_X^*R\bar j_{X*}\xrightarrow{Rh_!\epsilon_{\bar j_X}}Rh_!.$$
Then $C_u=i_Y^*d_u\circ B_{u,i_Y}^{-1}$. This is exactly the counit-defined formula in the specialization definition, now using its unbounded version. In case (ii), set $C_u=B_{u,q_Y}^{-1}$. All schemes needed for compact support are Noetherian: they are finite type over a field or a Noetherian trait; Nagata applies since the morphisms are separated finite type.

Work in ordinary unbounded derived categories. Constant-coefficient inverse image is additive and exact; open extension by zero is exact as well. Their termwise derived functors are therefore triangulated. Every module complex has a K-injective resolution, so the unbounded right-derived-functor theorem applies to $R\bar j_*$ and to each proper $Rr_*$. Equip each right adjoint with the shift structure determined by its left adjoint: the adjunction shift lemma makes both unit and counit shift-compatible, and the triangulated-right-adjoint theorem then gives exactness with these compatible shifts. Thus $T=i^*R\bar j_*$, $T=q^*$ and $Ru_!=Rr_*j_!$ are triangulated. For tensor, choose a K-flat resolution $P$ of the fixed input. The descended total tensor bifunctor is independent of this model. The total differential gives $P\otimes\operatorname{Cone}(f)\cong\operatorname{Cone}(P\otimes f)$: on the shifted summand of $P$-degree $p$ the identification has sign $(-1)^p$. Tensoring with $P$ preserves quasi-isomorphisms by K-flatness, so this cone identity descends to distinguished triangles. For the other variable, transport along the natural symmetry isomorphism $\sigma$ (Koszul sign $(-1)^{pq}$ in bidegree $(p,q)$): on $P^p\otimes C^{q+1}$ the shift identification of $P\otimes C[1]$ carries $(-1)^p$ and that of $C[1]\otimes P$ none, so $\sigma$ commutes with these identifications and $-\otimes^LN\cong N\otimes^L-$ as functors with shift; this gives exactness in the other variable. These arguments impose no lower bound on the complexes.

source.place: Tags 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor), 0A8D (lemma-adjoint-is-exact), 06YS (lemma-K-flat-resolution); agent application to ordinary unbounded derived functors and the total-tensor cone formula

proof.text: Use the shift structures of step 3 throughout. Pullback composition is induced termwise, and hence commutes with shifts. The open tensor comparison is induced by the sheaf tensor identity on direct-sum total complexes, so it commutes with their signed shift identifications. For the right-adjoint tensor map, transpose its shift-compatibility square: both paths become the tensor of the two counits, with the same tensor shift identification. Their equality follows from shift compatibility of those counits. Thus $t$ is shift-compatible in either input. All ordinary square mates, projection maps and the map $d_u$ of step 2 are composites and whiskerings of these comparisons, units and counits. The composition/whiskering lemma therefore makes them shift-compatible. The unbounded compact-support comparisons on a compactification are proper exchange followed by the degreewise open comparison; their composition and refinement comparisons have the adjunction normalizations stated in the cited compact-support theorem. They consequently have the same compatibility. If a shift-compatible comparison $\alpha$ is invertible, its shift equation $\varphi_2\alpha_{[1]}=\alpha[1]\varphi_1$ gives $\varphi_1\alpha_{[1]}^{-1}=\alpha[1]^{-1}\varphi_2$ by multiplication with the inverses. This covers the inverses used in $C_u$. Finally the shift-compatible-transformation lemma makes the three components of each transformation on a triangle a morphism of its image triangles. Step 3 says those triangles are distinguished. This proves the stated compatibility with derived cone triangles, also for tensor in either variable, on all the ambient unbounded inputs.

source.place: Tags 0144 (definition-triangle), 014V (definition-exact-functor-triangulated-categories), 014Y (lemma-composition-exact), 0A8D (lemma-adjoint-is-exact), 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition), 0F7L (lemma-base-change-shriek); agent unit/counit and shift-compatibility verification

proof.text:
For proper $u$ in (i), direct-image composition identifies
$$R\bar j_{Y*}Rh_*M=Ru_*R\bar j_{X*}M.$$
Applying proper base change along $i_Y$ gives $e_u:i_Y^*R\bar j_{Y*}Rh_*\xrightarrow{\sim}Ru'_*i_X^*R\bar j_{X*}$ on every unbounded input. By mate pasting this is the ordinary exchange obtained from $b_u$. In the counit-defined $d_u$, transpose this composite identification under $\bar j_Y^*\dashv R\bar j_{Y*}$: the transpose is exactly $Rh_*\epsilon_{\bar j_X}$ after the generic proper exchange. Thus step 2 gives $C_u=e_u^{-1}$. In (ii), proper base change along $q_Y$ gives $e_u=B_{u,q_Y}$, and the same assertion follows from the definition of $C_u$. The torsion-ring proper theorem applies to $A$, with no lower bound on its inputs.

If $u$ is smooth in (i), apply bounded-constructible smooth base change to the Cartesian square with vertical smooth map $u:X\to Y$ and horizontal $\bar j_Y:Y_{\bar\eta}\to Y$. The latter is qcqs (the geometric generic field extension is affine, as is the generic inclusion of the trait, and this remains so after base change). A power of $\ell$ annihilates $A$ and is invertible throughout. Hence $u^*R\bar j_{Y*}L\to R\bar j_{X*}h^*L$ is invertible for bounded constructible $L$, and exact restriction by $i_X^*$ gives invertible $b_u$. In (ii), $b_u$ is already the pullback-composition isomorphism, for arbitrary inputs.

The ordinary exchanges satisfy identities and composition by the mate-pasting formula and the associative pullback comparison. To check compact composition in (i), compare $d_{vu}$ with $d_v\circ Rv_!d_u$ using the compact-support composition identifications. Transpose both under $\bar j_Z^*\dashv R\bar j_{Z*}$. Compatibility of $B$ with compact composition makes their initial arrows the same. The transpose of the composite then inserts successively the counits for $\bar j_Y$ and $\bar j_X$; naturality moves $\epsilon_{\bar j_Y}$ past $\bar j_Y^*d_u$, and the triangle identity cancels the unit used to form $d_u$. What remains in both cases is $R(vh)_!\epsilon_{\bar j_X}$ after the generic exchange. Injectivity of adjunction proves equality. Pull back by $i_Z^*$ and use compatibility of $B_{-,i}$ with composition to obtain exactly $C_{vu}=C_v(Ru_!(-))\circ Rv'_!(C_u)$. The identity case uses the identity square and its counit--unit triangle. In (ii) the formula is the inverse of the stated composition law for $B$. Inverses of invertible exchanges inherit these equations by cancellation.

The monoidality and counit equations can be checked without any invertibility of $t$. For an ordinary square, transpose its exchange by the target direct-image adjunction: its transpose is the pullback-composition isomorphism followed by the source counit. Transposing its tensor-compatibility diagram therefore gives, on either path, the tensor of the two source counits, followed by the canonical pullback-composition identification. The equality follows from monoidality of composition and of the counit. Apply this first to the $\bar j$ square and then $i^*$ to obtain the displayed equation for $b_u$; apply it to the $u$ square and $R\bar j_*$ composition to obtain the displayed equation for $e_u$ and $\mu_u$. The transpose characterization of $e_u$ itself is
$$\epsilon_{u'}\circ u'^*e_u=T_X\epsilon_u\circ b_u(Ru_*(-)),$$
which is the requested ordinary counit formula. In (ii) the same calculation has $T=q^*$ and only pullback comparisons. These calculations use the tensor of counits, not invertibility of any lax tensorator.

For the projection equation in (ii), apply the unbounded compact projection/exchange identity with $v=q_Y$. Its exchange is $B$; multiply by its inverse $C_u$ and identify the pullback tensorators to get precisely the equation in the statement (switching the tensor factors by the symmetric tensor constraint). No projection isomorphism is needed. The same compact projection/exchange identity applies along $i_Y$ and $\bar j_Y$ in (i), on the chosen compactification and its base changes, for arbitrary complexes.

It remains to check the projection equation for $d_u$ before applying $i_Y^*$. Transpose its two paths under $\bar j_Y^*\dashv R\bar j_{Y*}$. Use step 9 to move the compact projection map through $B_{u,\bar j_Y}$. By the definition of the lax tensor map, its counit satisfies $\epsilon_{\bar j}(M\otimes N)\circ\bar j^*\mu=(\epsilon_{\bar j}M\otimes\epsilon_{\bar j}N)$ under pullback tensor identifications. The transpose characterization of the ordinary square defining $b$ similarly replaces its counit composite by $h^*\epsilon_{\bar j_Y}$. Thus both transposes are the same map
$$Rh_!\bar j_X^*R\bar j_{X*}M\otimes\bar j_Y^*R\bar j_{Y*}N
 \xrightarrow{\mathrm{PF}_h}Rh_!(\bar j_X^*R\bar j_{X*}M\otimes h^*\bar j_Y^*R\bar j_{Y*}N)
 \xrightarrow{Rh_!(\epsilon_{\bar j_X}M\otimes h^*\epsilon_{\bar j_Y}N)}Rh_!(M\otimes h^*N).$$
Naturality of projection in its two inputs justifies placing the two counits after this projection. Adjunction proves equality before restriction; projection/exchange along $i_Y$ then gives the exact displayed equation for $C_u$. This is a single two-counit calculation, with all exchanges and tensor maps fixed in steps 1--2.

source.place: 4.1.3(III)--(IV), 4.1.4(b); explicit adjunction verification of the projection square

proof.text: For the base trait, the germ isomorphism at its strictly henselian closed point identifies closed-point inverse image with global sections. This functor is exact, so on complexes it also identifies their derived functors. For $\bar j_B:\operatorname{Spec}\bar\eta\to B$, the separably closed point calculation gives $R\Gamma(\bar\eta,A)=A$ in degree zero. Composition of right derived direct images therefore yields $i_B^*R\bar j_{B*}A=A$. The unit sends each constant $a$ to itself, fixing the normalization. For a field extension, exact inverse image of the constant ring is the constant ring, giving $q^*A=A$ with the same normalization.

source.place: 1.3.3(a), 4.1.4(b); strict-local calculation of the base normalization

proof.text: Reduction maps are surjective closed immersions and hence universal homeomorphisms. Their small etale sites are equivalent; the constant-module inverse images are exact tensor equivalences. Transport across these equivalences identifies the sheaf adjunctions, including their units and counits, and hence their derived versions. In (i) use the reduced total scheme and the induced reductions of its fibres; these maps are surjective closed immersions even if reduction of a special fibre differs from the special fibre of the reduced total scheme. In particular all the intermediate nilpotent thickenings are identified by the same etale-site equivalence. Compactify and base change to compare compact support, using its refinement independence. Every $b,C,t,e$ above is built from these adjunctions and comparisons, so their formulas are preserved, including identities and composition. This changes schemes only, never the coefficient ring.

Let $B'\to B$ be a finite dominant map of strictly henselian traits with compatible geometric generic points, and put $r:Z_{B'}\to Z$. It is proper since finite. Using the discrete-valuation description of the local rings of traits, if $t,s$ are uniformizers of $B,B'$, then $t=vs^e$ for a unit $v$ and $e\ge1$. The algebraically closed residue field of $B$ has no proper finite residue extension, so $B'\times_B B_0$ is the local thickening $\operatorname{Spec}(\mathcal O_{B'}/(s^e))$ of $B_0$. Consequently the canonical closed inclusion $Z_0\to Z_{B'}\times_B B_0$ is a nilpotent closed immersion (its ideal is generated by $s$, with $s^e=0$); use step 12 to identify its etale category. The chosen geometric generic fibres identify and $r\bar j_{Z_{B'}}=\bar j_Z$. Proper base change along $i_Z$, together with direct-image composition, now gives
$$i_Z^*R\bar j_{Z*}=i_Z^*Rr_*R\bar j_{Z_{B'}*}\simeq Rr_{0*}i_{Z_{B'}\times_BB_0}^*R\bar j_{Z_{B'}*}\simeq\Psi_{Z_{B'}}.$$
The last equivalence uses that nilpotent closed immersion, not an assertion that the unreduced Cartesian closed fibre is $Z_0$.

The trait comparison in step 13 uses ordinary proper exchange, whose tensor and counit equations were proved in step 8. Its compatibility with $b$ follows by pasting the $r,u,\bar j,i$ squares. For $C$, paste the compact exchanges along $i$ and $\bar j$ in its definition, and then apply the same counit equation to $d_u$; the transposes on both sides are the generic compact exchange followed by $Rh_!\epsilon_{\bar j_X}$. The mate-pasting identity gives equality. For successive finite trait extensions the direct-image composition comparison and the pasting formula identify the composite with the comparison for the composite extension. This proves compatibility of the maps, rather than just equivalence of their source and target objects. For towers $F\subset K\subset L$ in (ii), monoidal pullback composition and compact exchange for composite base changes give the identical assertions directly. Together with step 12 this proves all the final compatibility clauses.

split_report.summary: Expanded the counit-defined exchanges into fourteen steps, proving the composition, tensor, projection and counit formulas on ordinary unbounded etale categories, with finite-trait and reduction comparisons. Reused existing nodes throughout; no new nodes and no statement change. Maintainer reader (2026-10-18) made the statement precise without changing its content: the compact-support projection map PF_u is now spelled out on a compactification (proper projection map of def-kun-projection-formula-map followed by the open tensor comparison of lem-pur-etale-open-derived-tensor), and 'trait' cites def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring; both added to stmt_deps.
